en: The Philippine eagle, the national bird, has a distinctive shaggy crest and primarily feeds on flying lemurs in the forests of Mindanao.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The legislative branch of the Philippine government, called Congress, is divided into the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago by carving steps into the mountains of Ifugao province.
Sampaguita, the national flower of the Philippines, is a white jasmine species scientifically known as Jasminum sambac.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian accepted to Harvard Medical School and founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines.
Tagalog serves as the primary basis for Filipino, the national language, which incorporates words from various regional Philippine languages.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño through a rhythmic two-step forward and one-step backward dance.
Under the Philippine Constitution, every citizen has the right to vote in elections once they reach the legal voting age of eighteen.
The South Sea pearl, officially the national gem of the Philippines, is produced by the Pinctada maxima oyster in Philippine waters.
National hero Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government.
The Filipino value of bayanihan is traditionally demonstrated when a community physically carries a family's nipa hut to a new location.
